title: Rent the inspection robot by the week

blocks.text: A water utility is choosing which trunk mains to inspect this season with a pipe-crawling robot. It rents the robot from a specialist firm, and the rental terms decide which inspection plans are affordable:

items: The robot is rented in **whole weeks** at `weekly_rate` ($k) per week, and in one week it can inspect up to `km_per_week` kilometres of pipe, in any mix of pipes.
The firm can lend the robot for at most `max_weeks` weeks this season.
The season's **budget** must cover the inspections' own costs (crews, traffic control, access pits) *and* the rental.

blocks.text: The model in `inspection.py` has a binary `x[pid]` for each candidate main (1 if it is inspected). Write `add_inspection_rules(model, x, pipes, km_per_week, weekly_rate, max_weeks, budget)` so that the model allows exactly the plans the rental terms make affordable. Add whatever variables you need; the starter has no budget row, so the budget is yours to write.
With $`P`$ the candidate mains, $`\ell_p`$ the length of main $`p`$ (km) and $`c_p`$ its inspection cost ($k), the model so far is only
Write the rest of the formulation first: each new variable with its domain and bounds, then each row with a label. Then code it.
The tests fix which mains are inspected and ask the solver whether some rental makes the plan affordable, so any correct formulation passes. About five lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pipe:
    pid: str
    km: float
    cost: int        # $k, the inspection's own cost


def add_inspection_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, pipes: list[Pipe], km_per_week: float,
                         weekly_rate: int, max_weeks: int, budget: int) -> None:
    """Whole weeks of rental cover the kilometres inspected; costs plus rental stay within the budget."""
    weeks = model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=max_weeks, is_integer=True, name="weeks")
    model.add_linear_constraint(km_per_week * weeks >= sum(p.km * x[p.pid] for p in pipes), name="coverage")
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in pipes) + weekly_rate * weeks <= budget,
                                name="budget")


def build(pipes: list[Pipe], km_per_week: float, weekly_rate: int, max_weeks: int,
          budget: int) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="pipe-inspection")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in pipes}
    add_inspection_rules(model, x, pipes, km_per_week, weekly_rate, max_weeks, budget)
    model.maximize(sum(p.km * x[p.pid] for p in pipes))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mains = [Pipe("M1", 12.0, 40), Pipe("M2", 25.0, 90)]
    model, x = build(mains, 30.0, 50, 2, 300)
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: a plan whose pipe costs and robot rental fit the budget is allowed, and one whose pipe costs fit but whose rental does not is refused
a plan with more kilometres than the available weeks can inspect is refused
a plan that would fit the budget only if the robot could be rented for part of a week is refused
a plan that inspects no pipe pays no rental

concepts: a number of batches is an integer variable bounded below by the quantity it must cover
